correctness.rationale: With the stated column convention the element condition is x=M sigma(x) for coefficientwise squaring sigma. Expansion in a cyclic normal basis turns that equation into v_j=M v_(j-1), and a choice of v_0 in ker(M^f−I) determines exactly one solution. This works even for singular M and when f is even. Repeated substitution kills the nilpotent Fitting summand; on the stable summand W the restriction B is invertible and sigma(x)=B^(-1)x. All geometric solutions are defined over F_(2^L) by this identity for L=ord(B); that field has exactly 2^r solutions by the normal-basis formula. The count reaches 2^r exactly when B^f=I, proving minimality. The zero-core case gives one geometric point and L=1. Frobenius orbit lengths divide L, and inversion of N_f=sum_(d|f) d c_d gives the claimed formal zeta product. In the cyclic formula, multiplication by a^f−1 modulo t^n−1 has kernel generated by (t^n−1)/gcd(t^n−1,a^f−1), so the nullity is the gcd degree without a squarefreeness requirement. For C5 the t=1 factor is killed by adjacency and on the remaining fifth-root factor a=t+t^(-1) solves a²+a+1=0. For Petersen M²=M+J and MJ=J give M³=M over F2. Binary elimination gives the respective odd and even nullities 5 and 6; the zeta factors follow. These are idempotent elements including zero, not idempotent multiplication operators or a graph Ihara zeta.

evidence: Set S=B sigma on the stable r-space. The quoted theorem gives an invertible geometric matrix P whose columns form an S-fixed basis, so the solution space is P F2^r. Because B is binary, sigma commutes with S and restricts to a binary linear operator C on this space. Since B sigma(P)=P, C=P^(-1)B^(-1)P. The nullity of C^f−I over F2 thus equals the nullity of B^f−I (similarity over the closure and invariance of rank under scalar extension). This gives every stated N_f. The order of C equals ord(B), so it also gives L, and the zeta is the standard finite permutation orbit product.

The graph evaluations need only the binary adjacency ranks; the C5 gcd and Petersen common-neighbor identity reduce them to routine finite matrix arithmetic. The distinct invariant is not rescued by a numeric value absent from a paper.

originality.rationale: The main claim is mathematically covered by a direct specialization of the established semilinear fixed-basis theorem plus the elementary nilpotent/stable decomposition. That theorem gives not just the size of the geometric set: in a fixed basis, arithmetic Frobenius is represented by a binary matrix similar to the inverse stable block, giving the exact entire rank tower, its order and the orbit zeta. The graph cases are parameter computations in this same result. There is also an explicit catalogue overlap at broader scope, independently of any inference about chronology from that record's later date. This is verified coverage, not a gap arising from unavailable literature.
residual_risks: No priority conclusion from catalogue dates. The exact binary complete-graph antecedent alluded to in the frozen text was not established. Other graph-specific publications were not exhaustively sought, which cannot undo the demonstrated implication.

value.rationale: Finite-extension point counts are a reasonable invariant for the named graph examples, and the frozen calculation can be useful exposition. But the claimed exact tower and zeta are mechanically implied by the prior fixed-basis theorem, and after that attribution the examples require only routine adjacency-matrix ranks. There is no independently supported nonmechanical graph invariant or further structural consequence in the frozen claim that survives this coverage.
residual_risks: This is not a rejection of point-counting questions for evolution algebras generally, nor of the importance of the named graphs. It is limited to the asserted arithmetic conclusions under the binary structure-matrix hypothesis.
